title: The Color of Fresh Is a Lie

copy.headline: That apple looks fresh because the store wants it to.
You have never once seen this store's food in its actual condition. Only its optimized one.
Produce misting systems spray a fine water mist every few minutes.
items: It makes vegetables look dewy and fresh.
It also adds water weight - you're paying per pound for water - and accelerates rot by introducing moisture to surfaces.

copy.headline: Apples in the produce section may be up to 12 months old.
items: Controlled-atmosphere storage (low oxygen, low temperature) suspends ripening.
A wax coating restores the shine.

copy.headline: Meat cases use specific lighting.
items: Red-spectrum lights make beef look redder and fresher.
Under neutral light, the same steak looks brown and dull.
copy.body: The meat hasn't changed. The light has.

copy.headline: Bakery items labeled "baked fresh today" may have arrived frozen and been reheated on-site.
items: The legal definition of "baked" includes finishing a par-baked product.
Fresh is a feeling, not a fact.

copy.headline: Misting, waxing, lighting, and labeling are all legal. None are disclosed at the point of sale.
copy.body: Freshness is a visual performance, not a guarantee.

copy.headline: The store shows you what it wants you to see.
copy.ctaLine: fond tracks what you actually bought and when it actually expires.
